examples.claim: The next model call after tool results is a recursive call inside the cycle, not an outer while loop
examples.source: strands.event_loop.event_loop API: 'Managing recursive calls for multi-turn tool interactions'; recurse_event_loop 'Make a recursive call to event_loop_cycle with the current state.'

examples.claim: Tool execution has four steps: validate against schema, locate in registry, execute with error handling, format as tool result
examples.source: Agent Loop: 'the execution system validates the request against the tool's schema, locates the tool in the registry, executes it with error handling, and formats the result as a tool result message.'

examples.claim: Default executor is ConcurrentToolExecutor (parallel); SequentialToolExecutor for guaranteed order (per Builder Center Part 1)
examples.source: Builder Center Part 1: 'By default, this is the ConcurrentToolExecutor, which runs all tools requested by the model in the same response in parallel ... there is also the SequentialToolExecutor for cases requiring guaranteed order.'

examples.claim: EventLoopStopEvent event['stop'] is a 7-tuple; item 7 is Checkpoint | None set when stop_reason == 'checkpoint'
examples.source: event_loop API: '(event["stop"]) is a 7-tuple ... Checkpoint | None: Checkpoint captured when stop_reason == "checkpoint"'
Quickstart 'pip install strands-agents'; package metadata of strands-agents 1.64.0 lists the 'otel' extra; command installs cleanly.

examples.claim: With turns=2 the turn-2 file write completes before the check, then the call stops with limit_turns and no final summary
examples.source: Agent Loop: tools requested by the previous turn always run before the check; reproduced with the SDK: stop_reason 'limit_turns', answer.txt exists, 2 model calls.

examples.claim: On Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google Gemini the total counts prompt-cache reads and writes in full
examples.source: Agent Loop: 'On Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini, that total counts prompt-cache reads and writes in full, so a cached turn uses as much of the limit as an uncached one.'

examples.claim: HookOrder.SDK_FIRST = -100, DEFAULT = 0 (implicit), SDK_LAST = 100; not enforced bounds; lower runs first
examples.source: Hooks: 'HookOrder.SDK_FIRST (-100) ... HookOrder.DEFAULT (0): implicit when no order is specified ... HookOrder.SDK_LAST (100) ... These are not enforced bounds'

examples.claim: Default retry: 6 total attempts (5 retries), first wait 4 s, doubling, max_delay 128 s; only ModelThrottledException
examples.source: Retry Strategies: 'retry throttling errors up to 5 times (6 total attempts) with exponential backoff starting at 4 seconds'; table max_attempts 6, initial_delay 4, max_delay 128.

examples.claim: Proactive compression is best-effort; if reduction throws or returns false the error is swallowed and the model call proceeds
examples.source: Conversation Management: 'Proactive compression is best-effort only, so if reduce() throws or returns false, the error is swallowed and the model call proceeds normally.'

examples.claim: With context_manager set, a co-provided conversation_manager is ignored; ContextManager owns overflow recovery and proactive compression; first-class parameter, not a plugin
examples.source: Context management: 'When context_manager is set, any co-provided conversation_manager is ignored. The ContextManager owns overflow recovery and proactive compression internally.' and 'first-class agent parameter, not a plugin.'

examples.claim: Handlers evaluate in registration order; Deny short-circuits; precedence deny > confirm > guide > transform > proceed
examples.source: Interventions: 'Handlers evaluate in registration order. If any handler returns Deny, remaining handlers are skipped' and 'well-defined precedence (deny > confirm > guide > transform > proceed).'

examples.claim: y/yes approves this call; t/trust approves later calls to the same tool while the agent lives; a negated tool cannot be trusted
examples.source: Approve before your agent acts: 'y or yes approves this call. t or trust approves this call and every later call to the same tool ...'; 'A negated tool always prompts and can't be trusted.'
